entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adolph Marx (1872–1956) was an American Catholic bishop who served as Bishop of Krishnagar in Bengal, India, representing the generation of foreign missionary bishops who built diocesan structures in British India during the colonial twilight and the transition to independence. A member of the Holy Cross Congregation, he worked in Bengal through the tumultuous decades of the Indian independence movement and Partition.

Bishop of Krishnagar from 1933, Marx led his diocese through the Bengal Famine of 1943—one of the twentieth century's worst humanitarian catastrophes, in which an estimated three million people died—and through Indian independence and the horrors of Partition in 1947. The Bengal Famine and Partition deeply scarred the Catholic communities of his diocese, which included significant Catholic populations among Bengali lower castes who had converted through the nineteenth-century mission.

His extended service in Bengal through these extraordinary crises illustrates the extraordinary demands placed on missionary bishops in colonial South Asia. After Indian independence, Marx continued in his role as the diocese began its transition toward indigenous leadership. His tenure represents the final phase of American Catholic missionary episcopate in British India, bridging the colonial era and the emerging indigenous Church.
